Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Ningbo ETDZ AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd"
Document: "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd."

"ETDZ" stands for Economic and Technological Development Zone (Ningbo Economic and Technological Development Zone). So the register version has "ETDZ" embedded, while the document says just "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd."

Wait, let me think about which is more likely the true legal name. The document is the certificate itself — the legal instrument. The document says "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd." The register says "Ningbo ETDZ AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd."

Hmm, actually many companies in Ningbo are registered in the Ningbo Economic and Technological Development Zone (ETDZ), and their legal names sometimes include "ETDZ" — e.g., "Ningbo ETDZ XXX Co., Ltd." But this could also be an artifact of data entry in the register, appending the zone to the name.

The rules say: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. Extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise) = document-noise with best_value from the register. Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is "ETDZ" an address fragment glued into a name? ETDZ = Economic and Technological Development Zone — a location/zone designation. It could be considered an address/location fragment. But it's also plausibly part of the legal company name: companies registered in development zones often legally include "ETDZ" in their name, e.g., "Ningbo Free Trade Zone XXX". Actually "Ningbo ETDZ AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd" — hmm.

Which is more likely correct? Let me look at real OIML certificates. R60/2017-A-NL1-22.02 from NMi Certin B.V., applicant Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd. Actually, I recall AIEN Electronics — load cell manufacturer in Yuyao, Ningbo. Their name: "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd" — address No. 66 Xiantan Road, Langxia Street, Yuyao City. Yuyao is not the ETDZ exactly; the Ningbo ETDZ is in Beilun/Xiaogang area. Langxia Street is in Yuyao. Hmm.

Actually wait — the document itself says "Applicant and Manufacturer Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd. No. 66 Xiantan Road, Langxia Street Yuyao City". So the document's own text supports "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd." as the name, with address "No. 66 Xiantan Road, Langxia Street, Yuyao City".

Now, which verdict? Options:

1. same-entity: The two names clearly refer to the same company (AIEN Electronics in Ningbo). The "ETDZ" is a descriptor. Per rules, spelling drift = same-entity, and best_value... For same-entity, the rule doesn't explicitly say which value; the "number/year format differences" clause says register canonical form. For same-entity generally, presumably we pick the best/canonical. The document is the legal instrument — so best_value should be the document's form? But the rule says "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." That's specific to numbers/years.

2. document-noise: If "ETDZ" in the register is an artifact — but the rule for document-noise says best_value from the register. That would keep "Ningbo ETDZ AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd". That seems wrong since the document is the legal instrument and it lacks ETDZ. Actually document-noise is about noise in the document, not the register. The register value here has ETDZ; the document doesn't. If anything, the register has the "noise" (ETDZ glued in?). The rules define document-noise as extraction artifacts — presumably artifacts introduced in the document extraction pipeline, with best_value from the register.

3. different-entity: They're clearly not different companies — same AIEN Electronics, Ningbo. So different-entity would be wrong.

So the verdict is same-entity (the names denote the same company; ETDZ is a zone descriptor / could be legal name variant). Best value: the document's, because the certificate is the legal instrument and the actual certificate text says "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd." The rules say for different-entity, best_value = document's. For same-entity, no explicit rule except number/year formats get register canonical. Here it's a name. Since the certificate is the legal instrument and the document text itself shows "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd.", the fused record should carry the document's value.

But wait — is "ETDZ" actually part of the legal name? Some sources list the company as "Ningbo ETDZ AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd." Hmm. Let me think. Searching memory: OIML certificate R60/2017-A-NL1-22.02 — I can't recall the actual entry. But real-world: AIEN Electronics (爱恩电子?) — Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd. Hmm, there is "Ningbo ETDZ Jinke Electronics" etc. Companies with "ETDZ" in legal names do exist. However, the certificate document itself — the authoritative legal instrument — lists the applicant as "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd." Also note page 1 says "Applicant and Manufacturer Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd." So the document is authoritative here.

But hold on — the comments in the document context are extraction pipeline comments: applicant: "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd" — that matches the visible text. So the document extraction is clean; the register's "ETDZ" is the deviation. Under the rules, that's not "document-noise" (that category is for artifacts in the document). It's best classified as same-entity (the ETDZ is a zone designation drift, not a different company) with best_value from the document since it's the legal instrument.

Alternatively, one could argue different-entity is too strong; same-entity fits. The instructions: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." ETDZ addition is more than spelling drift but not a genuinely different company name — it identifies the same company. "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity" — no, same company.

So verdict: same-entity; best_value: "Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd." (document form, since certificate is legal instrument and its own text confirms it).

One short sentence why: "Both denote the same company; 'ETDZ' is a zone-designation variant, and the certificate's own legal text gives 'Ningbo AIEN Electronics Co., Ltd.', so the fused record uses the document form."
